Three.js prompt: Single HTML file using three.js from CDN. Use an OrthographicCamera(-1,1,1,-1,0,1) with a single fullscreen PlaneGeometry(2,2) quad and a ShaderMaterial — this exact pairing is what makes the shader fill the whole canvas edge to edge. In the fragment shader, output color = palette(sin(uv.x*10 + t) + sin(uv.y*8 + t) + sin(length(uv-0.5)*15 + t*2)) using the standard cosine palette palette(x) = 0.5 + 0.5*cos(6.28318*(x + vec3(c0,c1,c2))) — choose your own (c0,c1,c2) phase offsets for whatever mood you want (warm, icy, acid, pastel...). Pass time as a uniform updated each frame in the animation loop.

Single HTML file using three.js from CDN. Fullscreen ShaderMaterial tunnel effect on an OrthographicCamera(-1,1,1,-1,0,1) quad. In the fragment shader center the UV as vec2 p = (uv - 0.5) * vec2(aspect, 1.0), then convert to polar: r = length(p), angle = atan(p.y, p.x). Build tiling coordinates tuv = vec2(angle/6.28318*repeatCount, 1.0/max(r,0.001) + time) and use tuv to tile any repeating pattern of your choice along the tunnel walls — could be hexagons, circuitry, alien glyphs, fractured crystal, organic cells, or something else entirely; pick whatever repeatCount (try 8-16) suits your pattern. Multiply the final color by 1.0/max(r,0.001) for perspective foreshortening and by smoothstep(0.9, 0.2, r) for a strong vignette toward the edges. Choose vivid, high-contrast colours. The only hard constraint: it must feel like flying through an infinite tunnel — everything else about the pattern and palette is yours to invent.

Single HTML file using three.js from CDN. Create 2000 stars as a THREE.Points object with random XY in [-1,1] and Z in [-1,-100]. Each frame add 0.3 to all Z values; when a star's Z > 0, respawn it at Z = -100 with new random XY. Use a PointsMaterial(color: 0xffffff, size: 0.05, sizeAttenuation: true) — sized so stars stay clearly visible as they approach without disappearing at the far end. PerspectiveCamera(75, aspect, 0.1, 200) at the origin looking down -Z; set the renderer's clear color to pure black so the white points read as bright pixels against it.

Single HTML file using three.js from CDN. Fullscreen ShaderMaterial (OrthographicCamera(-1,1,1,-1,0,1), 2x2 quad) that raymarches an SDF combining 4 moving spheres. Build the ray per pixel as if from a virtual camera: origin = vec3(0,0,4), direction = normalize(vec3((uv-0.5)*vec2(aspect,1.0), -1.5)). Combine the spheres with the polynomial smooth-min (numerically stable — do NOT use the exp/log version, it silently overflows to NaN/black when distances are large before the march converges): smin(a,b,k) { h = clamp(0.5+0.5*(b-a)/k, 0.0, 1.0); return mix(b,a,h) - k*h*(1.0-h); } with k=0.8. Sphere radius ~0.5 each; centers orbit the scene origin using sin/cos of time with different phases so they overlap and merge. March up to 64 steps, step = distance*0.9, stop when distance < 0.001 or total distance > 20 (shade background beyond that so the march can never hang). Estimate the surface normal from the SDF gradient (tetrahedron-offset trick) and shade with one directional light. Use a chrome-mercury palette: silvery blue-grey base, sharp white specular highlights, and a faint purple rim light on the dark side.

Single HTML file using three.js from CDN. Fullscreen ShaderMaterial fire simulation on an OrthographicCamera(-1,1,1,-1,0,1) quad. Build fbm from at least 5 octaves of a simple 2D value or noise function (define it inline — don't assume a built-in), with domain warping: sample the noise at uv + 0.4*noise(uv*3.0 + vec2(0.0, time*1.5)) to get roiling, organic flame shapes with tendrils and wisps. Shape the fire with a strong vertical profile — multiply density by smoothstep(1.0, 0.0, uv.y) so it's dense and blazing at the bottom (uv.y = 0) and thins to wisps near the top — plus a subtle horizontal sway via + 0.05*sin(time+uv.y*10.0) on the x sample. Map density through your own palette: not just orange — consider blue plasma, green witch-fire, purple demon flame, or white-hot solar flare. Add a brighter glowing ember layer for density > 0.8 near the base.

Single HTML file using three.js from CDN. Fullscreen ShaderMaterial on an OrthographicCamera(-1,1,1,-1,0,1) quad. In the fragment shader, center the UV, apply a rotation matrix with angle=time*0.3, then scale by (1.5 + sin(time)*0.7). Sample a procedural checker texture: mod(floor(p.x)+floor(p.y), 2.0), mixed between two contrasting colors of your choice. Use fract(p) before the floor so the pattern tiles infinitely in every direction.

Single HTML file using three.js from CDN. Fullscreen ShaderMaterial (OrthographicCamera(-1,1,1,-1,0,1), 2x2 quad). Build the ray as origin = vec3(0,0,5), direction = normalize(vec3((uv-0.5)*vec2(aspect,1.0), -1.5)). Fragment shader raymarches an SDF that unions a sphere (radius 0.6) and a box (half-extent 0.5) with the numerically-stable polynomial smooth-min smin(a,b,k){ h=clamp(0.5+0.5*(b-a)/k,0.0,1.0); return mix(b,a,h)-k*h*(1.0-h); }, k=0.3, then tile the whole SDF with mod(p, 4.0) - 2.0 so it repeats infinitely. March 80 steps, stop at hit threshold 0.001 or total distance 40 (shade fog beyond that so the march always terminates). Compute the normal via the tetrahedron offset trick. Shade with one directional light in a cool palette: deep navy fog fading to bright magenta where surfaces catch the light, plus a teal ambient term.

Single HTML file using three.js from CDN. Create a CanvasTexture by drawing scrolling text on a 2D canvas (redraw the canvas every frame with x offset = -time*100, and set texture.needsUpdate = true each time you redraw it — a forgotten needsUpdate is the single most common reason this effect appears frozen or blank). Apply the texture to a PlaneGeometry with many vertical segments (200x10). Use a custom vertex shader that displaces position.y by sin(position.x*0.5 + time*2)*0.3. OrthographicCamera looking at the plane, framed so the whole plane is in view. Draw the text in bright neon yellow on a deep purple background with a subtle horizontal scanline overlay; text content can be any short demoscene-style greeting.

Single HTML file using three.js from CDN. Stack 40 small BoxGeometry cubes (edge 1) along the Y axis from y=-20 to y=20. Each frame rotate cube[i] around Y by an angle = time + i*0.15 so the stack twists. Use MeshNormalMaterial (needs no lights). PerspectiveCamera positioned at roughly (30, 0, 30) looking at the origin so the full 40-unit-tall stack is in frame. Do not import OrbitControls from a separate CDN module unless you also add it to the importmap correctly — a slow auto-rotation of the camera around the stack is a simpler, equally effective alternative.

Single HTML file using three.js from CDN. THREE.Points with 5000 particles spawned at origin with random outward velocities and slight upward bias. Each frame: pos += vel*dt; vel.y -= gravity*dt; respawn particle when y < -10. Use AdditiveBlending, a small soft circular sprite texture drawn via canvas, and color particles by remaining lifetime.

Single HTML file using three.js from CDN. A 64x64 grid of unit BoxGeometry instances using InstancedMesh for performance (4096 individual Mesh objects will run too slowly and can trigger a low-FPS failure). Define a small inline 2D value-noise function yourself (don't assume a global noise2D exists) — e.g. hash the integer lattice corners with a sine/fract trick and bilinearly interpolate. For each cell set instance Y position to floor(noise2D(x*0.1, z*0.1)*8). Color each instance by its height through a blue -> green -> white gradient using setColorAt. Slowly orbit the camera around the center at a distance that keeps the whole 64x64 grid in view.

Single HTML file using three.js from CDN. Fullscreen ShaderMaterial (OrthographicCamera(-1,1,1,-1,0,1), 2x2 quad). Fragment shader iterates z = z*z + c where c = center + (uv-0.5)*vec2(aspect,1.0)*scale, center = vec2(-0.745, 0.1), and scale = 3.0*exp(-time*0.3) for a slow, never-ending zoom (scale never reaches exactly 0). Use up to 200 iterations, escape when dot(z,z) > 4.0; color by smooth iteration count (i - log2(log2(dot(z,z)))) through a sin-based palette of your choice.

Single HTML file using three.js from CDN. A central rotating MeshNormalMaterial torus knot lit only by its own material (no light needed). Draw a soft circular gradient onto a small canvas (radial gradient, white center fading to transparent) and use it as the texture for a bright AdditiveBlending Sprite placed at a position projected toward screen space, plus 6 smaller sprites of varying size/tint spaced evenly along the line from that position to screen center. Update every sprite's position each frame as the knot rotates.

Single HTML file using three.js from CDN. PlaneGeometry 20x20 with 200x200 segments, rotated -PI/2 on X. Custom vertex shader displaces position.z by the sum of 3 sine waves with different directions, frequencies, and time speeds. Use MeshPhongMaterial in a deep teal-to-cobalt water color with bright cyan specular highlights; one directional light from a low angle so peaks catch light sharply. Camera tilted down looking at the surface; dark navy background.

Single HTML file using three.js from CDN. 60 balls confined to a glowing 3D box, rendered with MeshPhongMaterial and per-ball randomised emissive colours. Gravity + elastic wall collisions + 0.98 restitution. Add visual spectacle: motion-blur trails on each ball (last 8 positions drawn as fading smaller spheres) and subtle colour cycling on each ball over time. Walls are near-transparent with visible wireframe edges. Dark background; let the glowing trails dominate. An UnrealBloomPass via EffectComposer is a nice finishing touch if you use it, but keep it optional — the scene must still look good with plain rendering if you skip it or the import fails.

Single HTML file using three.js from CDN. Start with an IcosahedronGeometry but make it interesting: animate the vertex positions over time (breathe, pulse, or morph between icosahedron and sphere using sin/cos displacement along vertex normals). Layer 3-5 nested instances at different scales, each counter-rotating at different speeds. Use additive blending on the LineSegments. Vary line colour or opacity per instance for a depth effect. Optional: add a particle cloud or bloom so the geometry appears to radiate energy. Avoid a plain rotation-only result.

Single HTML file using three.js from CDN. TubeGeometry along a CatmullRomCurve3 with 12 control points making a winding path; tube radius 1, 200 tubular segments. Apply a repeating CanvasTexture of alternating bright magenta and cyan stripes (procedurally drawn) and scroll its offset.x by time*0.5. Camera moves along the curve using position = curve.getPointAt(t) with t = (time*0.05) % 1, and must call camera.lookAt(curve.getPointAt((t + 0.01) % 1)) every frame so it always faces forward down the tube — without this the camera can end up looking sideways through the tube wall, which looks blank. Add a soft black vignette at the far end of the tunnel for depth.

Single HTML file using three.js from CDN. Fullscreen ShaderMaterial (OrthographicCamera(-1,1,1,-1,0,1), 2x2 quad). Fragment shader: center the UV, convert to polar (r, a) with a = atan(p.y,p.x), fold the angle into a wedge via a = abs(mod(a, 2.0*PI/N) - PI/N) with N=8, then rebuild p = r*vec2(cos(a),sin(a)) and sample a colorful procedural pattern from p (sums of sin(p*freq + time) work well). The folding produces 8-fold mirrored symmetry.

Single HTML file using three.js from CDN. 200 boids rendered as a single InstancedMesh of ConeGeometry (200 separate Mesh objects will tank the frame rate). Each frame apply three steering rules to each boid using simple squared-distance checks (no sqrt needed for the comparisons): separation (avoid neighbors within 1 unit), alignment (match average velocity within 3 units), cohesion (move toward neighbor center within 5 units). The O(n^2) neighbor loop over 200 boids is fine per frame as long as you don't also rebuild the whole geometry — only update the InstancedMesh matrices. Wrap positions inside a cube. Orient each boid along its velocity vector (e.g. quaternion.setFromUnitVectors). Color each boid by current speed through a cool palette (deep indigo when slow, bright cyan when fast). Dark navy background; faint wireframe cube showing the wrap bounds.

Single HTML file using three.js from CDN plus EffectComposer (import RenderPass, ShaderPass, and EffectComposer all from the same three.js addons path you put in the importmap). Render a rotating MeshNormalMaterial torus knot via a RenderPass, then add a custom ShaderPass whose fragment shader: (a) shifts the R and B channels horizontally by small offsets that change each frame — texture2D(tDiffuse, uv + vec2(offset,0.0)).r — (b) every few frames replaces random horizontal slices with the source sampled at a different y offset. Drive both effects by a time uniform you update each frame. Call composer.render() instead of renderer.render() in the animation loop, and make sure the composer is resized on window resize.

Single HTML file using three.js from CDN with EffectComposer and UnrealBloomPass (import both from the same three.js addons path used in your importmap, and call composer.render() in the animation loop — not renderer.render()). A TorusKnotGeometry with MeshBasicMaterial color 0xff3399 for an emissive feel. RenderPass + UnrealBloomPass(new THREE.Vector2(width,height), strength 1.5, radius 0.6, threshold 0.0). Rotate the knot slowly. Black background so bloom dominates.

Single HTML file using three.js from CDN. PlaneGeometry 200x200 with 256x256 segments, rotated -PI/2 on X. Define a small inline 2D value-noise function yourself (hash lattice corners, bilinear interpolate) and combine 3 octaves of it in a vertex shader to displace position.z. Camera at height 5 moving forward along -Z each frame at constant speed; add the camera's Z offset into the noise sample coordinate so the terrain appears infinite rather than static. Color terrain by height (the displaced z, passed to the fragment shader as a varying): dark olive in valleys, tan on slopes, bright snow-white on the peaks. Tint the depth fog a warm pink-orange for a sunset feel.

Single HTML file using three.js from CDN. Fullscreen ShaderMaterial (OrthographicCamera(-1,1,1,-1,0,1), 2x2 quad). Fragment shader draws 8 horizontal bars whose vertical centers are cy_i = sin(time + i*phase)*0.4 + 0.5 for i in 0..7. For each bar add smoothstep(0.06, 0.0, abs(uv.y - cy_i)) * barColor_i to the output color (0.06 controls bar thickness — tune to taste), where each bar has its own highlight-to-shadow gradient (e.g. blue, red, gold) blended vertically within its band.

Single HTML file using three.js from CDN. Fullscreen ShaderMaterial simulating SNES Mode 7 (OrthographicCamera(-1,1,1,-1,0,1), 2x2 quad). Fragment shader: for pixels below the horizon line, compute ground-plane world coordinates by perspective-dividing by (uv.y - horizonY) — i.e. treat 1.0/(uv.y - horizonY) as depth — scroll those coordinates by time, and sample a procedural checker in alternating bright red and white squares. Above the horizon line, output a sky gradient from peach-orange at the horizon to deep violet at the zenith.

Single HTML file using three.js from CDN. 64 BoxGeometry bars in a row acting as a fake frequency analyzer driven entirely by math (no audio input). For bar i (0..63), scale.y = 0.3 + abs(sin(time*1.3 + i*0.2) + sin(time*2.1 + i*0.31)*0.6 + sin(time*3.7 + i*0.11)*0.4) — never let scale.y reach exactly 0 or the bar disappears entirely. Color each bar with color.setHSL(i/64, 1.0, 0.5) so hue sweeps red -> orange -> yellow -> green -> cyan -> blue -> violet left to right. Set scene.background to pure black (0x000000) explicitly — a default transparent canvas will wash out the neon look. Additive glow sprites behind each bar are a nice optional touch for a neon-club feel.

Single HTML file using three.js from CDN. Self-playing Breakout: 8 rows by 14 columns of brick BoxGeometry instances at the top, a paddle PlaneGeometry at the bottom, and a SphereGeometry ball with constant-speed velocity (keep speed magnitude fixed even after bounces, only change direction). Each frame paddle.x += (ball.x - paddle.x)*0.12 so it tracks the ball. Use simple axis-aligned bounding-box checks for collisions: reflect velocity.x when the ball's box overlaps a wall, velocity.y when it overlaps the paddle or a brick top/bottom; remove the brick on hit. Color bricks by row through a rainbow palette. Reset the whole level when bricks are empty or the ball drops below the paddle. OrthographicCamera framed to the play field.

Single HTML file using three.js from CDN. Two paddle PlaneGeometry meshes on left and right, a SphereGeometry ball, and a dashed center line drawn as LineSegments. Each frame both paddles lerp paddle.y toward ball.y with factor 0.07 plus a small random jitter so neither side wins instantly; clamp paddle.y so it can't move off the top/bottom of the field. Ball reflects off top/bottom walls and off paddles when their bounding boxes overlap; ball speed multiplies by 1.05 on each paddle hit, capped at some maximum so it never gets uncontrollably fast. Score rendered above as a CanvasTexture. OrthographicCamera. Render bright white paddles and ball on a deep black background with a soft cyan glow on the dashed center line and a faint cyan trail behind the ball.

Single HTML file using three.js from CDN. Implement the classic GPU ping-pong pattern precisely: create two THREE.WebGLRenderTarget(128, 128, { type: THREE.FloatType }) targets, A and B. Seed target A by rendering one pass of a shader that outputs random 0/1 values (30% live) to it. Each frame: render a fullscreen quad whose fragment shader reads the CURRENT target's texture, samples the 8 Moore neighbors at integer texel offsets (1.0/128.0 in UV space), applies Conway's B3/S23 rule, and writes the next generation — but render this INTO the OTHER target, then swap which target is "current" for next frame (classic ping-pong; rendering a target into itself produces undefined/blank results). Finally render the current target's texture to the screen with a second fullscreen quad, mapping alive=neon green, dead=black. Reseed with new random noise every 30 seconds. OrthographicCamera, fullscreen quads.

Single HTML file using three.js from CDN. A SphereGeometry bird with constant rightward camera scroll; vertical velocity affected by gravity each frame. Generate pipe pairs (two BoxGeometry rectangles with a gap) every 200 units ahead at random gap centers. Each frame the AI flaps (velocity.y = +6) only if bird.y is below the next pipe-gap-center minus a small margin. Reset world on collision with a pipe or floor. OrthographicCamera, parallax sky background. Use a golden-yellow bird, bright green pipes with darker green caps, and a sky gradient from light cyan at the bottom to deeper blue at the top; rolling white cloud silhouettes drift slowly in the background.

Single HTML file using three.js from CDN. Represent the game state as a plain 2D array (30x30) marking empty/snake/food cells, separate from the three.js meshes. Snake is a chain of small BoxGeometry segments, food is a red sphere at a random empty cell. Each move, run a standard queue-based breadth-first search from the head to the food over the array (4-directional, skipping snake-body cells) to get the next direction; if no path exists, fall back to any move that doesn't immediately hit a wall or the snake's own body. Step every 100 ms; grow on eating, and rebuild the mesh positions from the array after every step. OrthographicCamera, top-down view.

Single HTML file using three.js from CDN. 10x20 well of unit BoxGeometry cells, tracked as a plain 2D array separate from the meshes. Spawn the standard 7 tetrominoes using simple 90-degree matrix rotations (no SRS wall-kick system needed — if a rotation would overlap the well or filled cells, just skip that rotation as a candidate). For the current piece, try every combination of rotation (0/90/180/270) and x position; for each, drop it straight down to its resting row and score the result with -aggregateHeight - 4*holes + linesCleared*2 - bumpiness; keep the best-scoring placement, then animate the piece sliding/rotating into place over a fraction of a second. Clear filled rows with a quick flash before collapsing rows above. Color pieces by classic Tetris colors. OrthographicCamera.

Single HTML file using three.js from CDN. Keep asteroids and bullets in plain JS arrays of small objects (position, velocity, size), each with a paired Line mesh you keep in sync every frame — don't try to manage this purely through three.js scene graph queries. White wireframe Line meshes for asteroids (random irregular polygons) and a triangular ship that auto-aims at the nearest asteroid, thrusts toward it, and fires a Line bullet every 400 ms. On bullet hit, remove the hit asteroid from the array and, if it was large, push two new smaller asteroids (half the radius) into the array with randomized outward velocities; when an asteroid is already at the smallest size, just remove it. Wrap all positions toroidally on a fixed-size playfield (if x < -bound, set x = bound, and similarly for y). OrthographicCamera, black background.

Single HTML file using three.js from CDN. Represent the maze as a plain 2D array (28x16) of wall/open cells, separate from the BoxGeometry wall meshes and pellet spheres built from it. A yellow disc agent picks the nearest reachable pellet via breadth-first search over the array each step and moves one cell toward it per tick. Two ghost agents: give each a simple 2-state behavior that alternates every 7 seconds — "chase" (BFS toward the player agent) and "scatter" (move toward a fixed corner of the maze) — this is much easier to get right than more elaborate ghost AI and still reads correctly. On ghost contact, reset all agent positions; when all pellets are eaten, regenerate the pellet layout. OrthographicCamera, top-down.

Single HTML file using three.js from CDN. On a 20x20x20 integer grid, track pipe growth with a plain 3D occupancy array. Spawn pipe segments as CylinderGeometry between adjacent grid cells: to orient a cylinder from cell A to cell B, position it at the midpoint and use quaternion.setFromUnitVectors(THREE.Object3D.DEFAULT_UP, direction.normalize()) so it points the right way — a cylinder left at its default upright orientation will look wrong or invisible end-on. Step into a random unblocked neighbor each tick; place a SphereGeometry elbow at every direction change. Use random saturated MeshPhongMaterial colors per pipe with one DirectionalLight plus ambient light (Phong materials render black with no light in the scene). When a pipe gets stuck, start a new one from a random free cell. Slowly orbit the camera.

Single HTML file using three.js from CDN. Two polygons of 4 points each bouncing inside a 2D rectangle (each point has a velocity, reverses on wall hit). Each frame draw the last 30 polygon snapshots as Line meshes with hue rotating over time and opacity fading with age (this is the classic Windows 3.1 Mystify look — straight-edged trailing polygons, not literal bezier curves, despite the name). OrthographicCamera, additive blending, black background.

Single HTML file using three.js from CDN. 5 emitter points orbit the origin on different orbits. Each emitter spawns ~50 particles per second as THREE.Points with AdditiveBlending and a soft circular canvas sprite. Give particles a curl-noise-like velocity using an easy analytic formula: vx = sin(y*freq + time) - sin(z*freq), vy = sin(z*freq + time) - sin(x*freq), vz = sin(x*freq + time) - sin(y*freq) (this behaves like curl noise without needing real gradient noise). Color per emitter (cyan, magenta, gold, lime, white). Create long fade trails by setting renderer.autoClear = false and drawing a translucent black fullscreen quad each frame before drawing the particles.

Single HTML file using three.js from CDN. Generate a 16x16 maze using recursive backtracking: start from a random cell, and while it has unvisited neighbors, pick one at random, knock down the wall between them, and recurse; when stuck, backtrack to the last cell that still has an unvisited neighbor. Render walls as BoxGeometry instances. The camera walks the corridors in first person: at each junction pick a random unvisited-preferred corridor and smoothly turn over 0.5s by slerping the camera's facing quaternion (not teleporting the rotation instantly). Use stone gray walls with a subtle vertical brick texture; floor in warm brown tiles; ceiling near-black. One warm amber PointLight follows the camera (torch-like). Add a deep blue exponential fog for depth.

Single HTML file using three.js from CDN. ~20 boxy toaster meshes (assemble per instance from BoxGeometry: body + slot + 2 flapping wing PlaneGeometry pieces) drift diagonally from upper-right to lower-left. Wings flap with sin(time*8 + phase). Mix in a few brown BoxGeometry slices of toast. Re-spawn off-screen toasters at the upper-right edge once they drift past the lower-left edge of the camera frustum. Soft blue gradient background.

Single HTML file using three.js from CDN. 30 fish, each a small ellipsoid (scaled SphereGeometry) with a triangular tail PlaneGeometry attached at the fish's rear and hinged so it wags via rotation.y = sin(time*5 + phase)*0.5. Fish swim along sine paths with random amplitudes; when a fish nears a tank edge, steer its heading back toward the center rather than clipping through the wall. Orient each fish to face its direction of travel. Add seaweed strands (PlaneGeometry with vertex-shader sway), bubbles as rising THREE.Points, and a subtle blue-green caustic shader on the floor.

Single HTML file using three.js from CDN. Implement a 2D iterated function system with GPU accumulation. Set up two THREE.WebGLRenderTarget(1024,1024,{type:THREE.FloatType}) targets for ping-pong accumulation, cleared to black once at startup. Each frame: run a batch of a few thousand points (not all points at once — spread the workload across frames so it stays fast) through a randomly chosen affine transform plus a nonlinear variation (sinusoidal: (sin(x),sin(y)); spherical: (x,y)/(x*x+y*y+eps); or swirl), and render them as additive-blended gl.POINTS into the CURRENT accumulation target while reading nothing from it (accumulation only ever adds, never reads its own target in the same pass). Every frame, display the accumulation texture to the screen via a second fullscreen quad using log(1.0 + accumulatedValue) to compress the huge dynamic range, mapped through a hue palette. Slowly mutate the transform parameters over many seconds.

Single HTML file using three.js from CDN. Integrate the Lorenz system (sigma=10, rho=28, beta=8/3) with RK4 at dt=0.005, ~100 steps per frame. Append each point to a BufferGeometry Line; cap the trail at 8000 vertices (rolling buffer). Color along the path by t through an HSL palette. The attractor spans roughly [-25,25] in x/y and [0,50] in z, so position the camera around distance 80-100 from the origin (e.g. (60,60,40)) looking at (0,0,25) so the whole shape is in view, then slowly orbit it. Black background.

Single HTML file using three.js from CDN. Plot the Clifford attractor x_next = sin(a*y) + c*cos(a*x), y_next = sin(b*x) + d*cos(b*y) with a=-1.4, b=1.6, c=1.0, d=0.7. Set up a single THREE.WebGLRenderTarget(1024,1024,{type:THREE.FloatType}) as an accumulation buffer, cleared to black once at startup — do not clear it every frame, or nothing accumulates. Each frame, iterate a batch of a few thousand points (spread the full 200000 points across many frames rather than computing them all at once) and render them as additive-blended gl.POINTS into that target. Every frame, display the target's texture to the screen via a second fullscreen quad, mapping density through log(1.0 + density) and a viridis-like palette so both faint and dense regions stay visible. Every 20s, smoothly interpolate (a,b,c,d) toward a new random preset AND clear the accumulation buffer at that moment so the old and new attractor shapes don't smear together.

Single HTML file using three.js from CDN. Place 1500 seeds at polar (r, theta) = (sqrt(i)*spacing, i*137.5deg) for i in 0..1499, rendered as a single InstancedMesh of CircleGeometry — 1500 individual Mesh objects will run too slowly and can trigger a low-FPS failure. Color each instance by i through a sunflower yellow to orange gradient using setColorAt. Slowly increase spacing over time and spin the whole arrangement (rotate the InstancedMesh, don't recompute positions) so the seed-head pattern emerges and breathes. OrthographicCamera.

Single HTML file using three.js from CDN. Define a target shape as a polyline of 2D points (e.g. sample the outline of the letter A as a list of (x,y) pairs). Compute its discrete Fourier coefficients directly by the DFT sum: for each frequency k, c_k = (1/N) * sum_n point[n] * exp(-2πi*k*n/N), evaluated as separate real/imaginary sums since GLSL/JS have no complex numbers built in. Each frame draw N nested rotating circles as Line meshes where circle k has radius |c_k| and rotates at angular speed k (attached tip-to-tip, each circle's center at the previous circle's tip); trace the path of the final tip with a fading Line. Start N at 8 and grow it toward 64 over time by adding more circles. OrthographicCamera. Render the rotating circles in soft cool blues and greys; the traced tip path glows bright hot pink and slowly fades to magenta. Black background.

Single HTML file using three.js from CDN. Generate parametric points x = (R-r)*cos(t) + d*cos((R-r)/r * t), y = (R-r)*sin(t) - d*sin((R-r)/r * t) for t in 0..200*PI; render as a Line. Slowly mutate (R, r, d) and rotate the result. Color by t through HSL hue. OrthographicCamera.

Single HTML file using three.js from CDN. Recursively pack circles using Descartes' Circle Theorem: for three mutually tangent circles with curvatures k1,k2,k3, a fourth tangent circle has curvature k4 = k1+k2+k3 ± 2*sqrt(k1*k2+k2*k3+k3*k1) (its center follows the analogous complex-number formula) — pick the smaller positive root to nest inward. Start from 3 mutually tangent parent circles and recurse 6 levels deep. Render each circle as a Line (32+ segments each). Color by recursion depth through a cool palette. Slowly rotate and breathe-zoom the whole pattern. OrthographicCamera.

Single HTML file using three.js from CDN. Implement the GPU ping-pong pattern precisely: create two THREE.WebGLRenderTarget(256, 256, { type: THREE.FloatType }) targets, A and B. Seed target A with a single 1.0 pixel at the center column of its bottom row, all else 0. Each frame: render a fullscreen quad whose fragment shader reads the CURRENT target, and for the row one texel above y=0 (i.e. shift the whole image up by one texel: new pixel at row y = old pixel at row y-1 for y>0), computes Wolfram Rule 30 from the 3 texels directly below it in the OLD image at row 0, and writes the result into row 0 of the OTHER target — then swap which target is "current". This must render into the other target, never into itself, or the pattern won't update. Every frame, display the current target as black-on-white pixels via a second fullscreen quad. OrthographicCamera, fullscreen quads, nearest-neighbor filtering for crisp pixels.

Single HTML file using three.js from CDN. Two ping-pong pairs of THREE.WebGLRenderTarget(512,512,{type:THREE.FloatType}) storing concentrations U (init 1.0 everywhere) and V (init 0.0, with a small 50x50 noisy patch of ~0.5 in the center). Each frame run a Gray-Scott step with the standard 4-neighbor (not diagonal) discrete Laplacian: lap(X) = X_up + X_down + X_left + X_right - 4.0*X_center (sampled at 1-texel offsets), using diffusion rates Du=1.0, Dv=0.5, f=0.0367, k=0.0649, dt=1.0: U' = U + (Du*lap(U) - U*V*V + f*(1.0-U))*dt, V' = V + (Dv*lap(V) + U*V*V - (f+k)*V)*dt. Render into the OTHER target each step and swap, never sampling and writing the same target in one pass. Display V through a teal-to-cream palette. These exact constants are tuned to be stable and reliably produce spots-and-stripes patterns — avoid inventing different rate constants, small changes here can make the simulation diverge to solid black or white.

Single HTML file using three.js from CDN. Simulate a chaotic double pendulum: masses m1=m2=1, rod lengths L1=L2=1, gravity g=9.8. Use these exact equations of motion (deriving them from scratch is genuinely error-prone — use these): with theta1,theta2 the angles from vertical and w1,w2 their angular velocities, delta = theta1-theta2, den = 2*m1+m2-m2*cos(2*delta): w1' = (-g*(2*m1+m2)*sin(theta1) - m2*g*sin(theta1-2*theta2) - 2*sin(delta)*m2*(w2*w2*L2+w1*w1*L1*cos(delta))) / (L1*den); w2' = (2*sin(delta)*(w1*w1*L1*(m1+m2) + g*(m1+m2)*cos(theta1) + w2*w2*L2*m2*cos(delta))) / (L2*den). Integrate with RK4 at dt=0.0001, about 100 substeps per frame (100 substeps is enough for visible smooth chaos without costing too much per-frame CPU time — do not go far beyond this or the frame rate will suffer). Render rods as Lines, masses as small spheres. Trail the second mass with a 4000-vertex rolling Line whose hue advances with time. OrthographicCamera.

Single HTML file using three.js from CDN. Define a 2D analytic field, e.g. (sin(y) + cos(x*0.5 + t), sin(x) - cos(y*0.5 + t)). Spawn 1500 THREE.Points; each frame advect each point by the field at its position with dt=0.016. Re-seed a point at a new random position when its speed stays below 0.05 for more than 60 consecutive frames, or when it drifts outside a fixed bounding box (e.g. +/-15 units). Color by current speed. Create faint trails by setting renderer.autoClear = false and drawing a low-opacity black fullscreen quad each frame before drawing the points.

Single HTML file using three.js from CDN. 4000 THREE.Points seeded in a thin disk with circular orbital velocity around a central heavy mass. Use simple, robust physics rather than a full far-field approximation: each frame, apply one central gravitational attraction per particle toward the galaxy center (F = -G*M/r^2, softened as F = -G*M/(r^2+eps) to avoid a singularity at r=0), plus a mild outward pressure term proportional to local particle density in, say, a coarse 16x16 grid of bins (count particles per bin, push particles in crowded bins slightly outward) so the disk doesn't collapse into a single point over time. Integrate with leapfrog at dt=0.01. Color by speed; AdditiveBlending; slow camera tilt.

Single HTML file using three.js from CDN. Parametric curve x = sin(a*t + p), y = sin(b*t + q), z = sin(c*t + r) for t in 0..2PI with ~3000 samples; render as TubeGeometry. (a,b,c) start at small integers and slowly drift, morphing the figure through Lissajous knots — rebuild the TubeGeometry only every few frames (not every single frame) since it drifts slowly and geometry rebuilding is relatively costly. Rainbow tube color along the path; auto-rotate.

Single HTML file using three.js from CDN. Generate a P3 (rhombus) Penrose tiling by deflating Robinson triangles rather than whole rhombs — it's the more mechanical, less error-prone way to do this: represent each half-rhomb as a triangle tagged 'thin' or 'thick' with 3 vertices; a fixed substitution rule replaces each thin triangle with 2 smaller triangles and each thick triangle with 3 smaller triangles, computed purely from linear interpolation between the parent's existing vertices (no trigonometry needed after the first generation). Start from a 'sun' configuration of 10 thin triangles arranged in a circle and recurse 5 times. Merge triangle pairs back into rhombs for rendering as flat ShapeGeometry; color thick rhombs in a warm rust orange and thin rhombs in deep teal, with a thin black outline on every tile. Slowly rotate. OrthographicCamera.

Single HTML file using three.js from CDN. L-system axiom F, rule F -> FF+[+F-F-F]-[-F+F+F]; iterate 5 times. Interpret turtle: F draw a segment, +/- yaw by 22.5 degrees, [/] push/pop state with a small random 3D twist (a few degrees of extra random pitch/roll) on each branch so it doesn't look perfectly flat. Render branches as CylinderGeometry instances tapering with depth (thicker near the trunk, thinner at the tips); leaves at terminals as small green PlaneGeometry billboards. Sway each branch with sin(time + depth) for wind.

Single HTML file using three.js from CDN. L-system axiom F++F++F, rule F -> F-F++F-F, angle 60deg; iterate 5 times. Each iteration multiplies the segment count by 4 and should scale the segment length down by 1/3 (start with an initial segment length such as 8, divided by 3 for every iteration) — without this scaling the curve's total size explodes and can end up entirely outside the camera view, which looks blank. Render as a single Line through the resulting points, using an OrthographicCamera framed to roughly [-6,6] in both axes (the properly-scaled curve fits comfortably inside that). Slowly rotate and pulse line color through a cyan-to-white palette. Optional: animate iteration count from 0 to 5 to watch it grow.

Single HTML file using three.js from CDN. This is a static-shape effect with a slow parameter drift, not a per-frame simulation — structure it as such. Once at startup, iterate Barnsley's 4-affine-map IFS for 100000 points and upload them into a single static BufferGeometry of THREE.Points (small, green, slight per-axis color shift). Every few seconds (not every frame), nudge one coefficient of one of the 4 transforms by a small random amount, then regenerate the 100000-point buffer and update the BufferGeometry's position attribute (recomputing 100000 points every single frame will make the frame rate collapse — only do it on that slow interval). Slowly rotate the fern continuously between regenerations. OrthographicCamera.

Single HTML file using three.js from CDN. Generate the Heighway Dragon via L-system: axiom FX, rules X -> X+YF+, Y -> -FX-Y, angle 90deg; iterate 14 times. Render as a single Line with hue along the path. Animate by drawing the path progressively over 10s, then fade and restart at a new rotation.

Single HTML file using three.js from CDN. Recursively generate the 3D Hilbert space-filling curve at order 4 (~4096 points). Render as TubeGeometry along a CatmullRomCurve3 of those points; rainbow color along the tube. Slowly orbit the camera; pulse tube radius with sin(time).

Single HTML file using three.js from CDN. Recursively subdivide a regular tetrahedron 5 levels deep: at each level, replace one tetrahedron with 4 smaller ones, each half-scale, positioned at the original tetrahedron's 4 vertices and the midpoints between them — concretely, for parent vertices A,B,C,D the 4 children are the tetrahedra formed at corners A, B, C, D with their other 3 vertices being the midpoints of the edges from that corner (e.g. child at A uses A, midpoint(A,B), midpoint(A,C), midpoint(A,D)). Render the leaf tetrahedra with an InstancedMesh of TetrahedronGeometry, colored by a small palette varied with recursion depth. Slowly rotate; one DirectionalLight.

Single HTML file using three.js from CDN. Fullscreen ShaderMaterial (OrthographicCamera(-1,1,1,-1,0,1), 2x2 quad). Build a view ray per pixel: direction = normalize(vec3((uv-0.5)*vec2(aspect,1.0), -1.0)). Fragment shader raymarches at most 48 steps along that ray (48 keeps this affordable; going much higher risks a low-FPS failure) sampling a 4-octave fbm of value noise (define the value-noise function yourself) to get density; accumulate density*stepSize into an alpha value and stop early once alpha exceeds ~0.95. For self-shadowing, take just 4 extra samples toward the sun direction at the point of highest density (a full second raymarch per pixel is too expensive) and darken by the accumulated density found there. Blend the cloud color over a sky gradient from horizon to zenith. Slowly translate the noise sample point with time so clouds drift.

Single HTML file using three.js from CDN. Fullscreen ShaderMaterial (OrthographicCamera(-1,1,1,-1,0,1), 2x2 quad). Define a small inline fbm function yourself: sum 3 octaves of a 2D value-noise (hash lattice corners, bilinear interpolate), each octave at double the frequency and half the amplitude of the last. Use the fbm as a height field, compute its gradient via central differences (sample height at uv+eps and uv-eps on each axis) for a fake normal, and use a thin-film palette vec3(0.5)+0.5*cos(2*PI*(c*t+d)) keyed off (dot(normal, viewDir) + height*5) where viewDir = vec3(0,0,1). Animate by adding time to the noise input coordinate.

Single HTML file using three.js from CDN. Fullscreen ShaderMaterial. Fragment shader perturbs UV by sin/cos of (uv*freq + time), computes the minimum distance to a set of moving feature points (Voronoi-like), then accumulates pow(1-d, 60) over 3 layers. Tint blue-green and add a subtle vignette.

Single HTML file using three.js from CDN. Fullscreen ShaderMaterial (OrthographicCamera(-1,1,1,-1,0,1), 2x2 quad). Convert UV to polar (r, a) with r = length(p) (clamp r to a minimum of 0.001 before feeding it to log() — log(0) produces NaN, which reads as a black hole of pixels at the exact center of the screen). Spiral arm intensity = pow(0.5+0.5*cos(2*a + log(max(r,0.001))*6 + time*0.2), 8) * exp(-r*1.5). Mix in dust lanes via fbm noise (define a small inline fbm yourself); bright core via exp(-r*8). Color through a hot-core to pink to blue palette.

Single HTML file using three.js from CDN. Fullscreen ShaderMaterial (OrthographicCamera(-1,1,1,-1,0,1), 2x2 quad) that raymarches an SDF smooth-minning 6 spheres whose centers move on slow vertical sine paths with phase offsets. Use the numerically-stable polynomial smooth-min (not the exp/log version, which can overflow to NaN/black when distances are large early in the march): smin(a,b,k){ h=clamp(0.5+0.5*(b-a)/k,0.0,1.0); return mix(b,a,h)-k*h*(1.0-h); }, k=0.8. March up to 64 steps, stop at hit threshold 0.001 or total distance 20. Shade with one warm point light from below. Background dark red to amber gradient. The smin produces classic merging blobs.

Single HTML file using three.js from CDN. Fullscreen ShaderMaterial. Fragment shader: for each pixel start a 2D ray from the camera, and over 60 steps integrate a simple inverse-square pull toward the screen-center black hole, softened as pull = strength / (r*r + 0.05) so the ray direction update never divides by a near-zero r, then sample a procedural starfield (hash-based dots) at the bent direction. Add a thin accretion disk by checking if the bent ray crosses the y=0 plane within radii r_in..r_out. The void is pure black with a faint deep-purple Einstein ring; the accretion disk glows hot orange near the inner edge fading to white at the outer edge; starfield in cool blue-white. Slow camera drift.

Single HTML file using three.js from CDN. Render large pixel-style text on a CanvasTexture mapped to a tall plane that scrolls horizontally (offset.x decreases with time; remember to set texture.needsUpdate = true whenever you redraw the canvas). The plane has 200 vertical segments; a vertex shader sin-warps position.y by 0.4*sin(position.x*0.5 + time*2). For the scroll text content: please write your own ~500-word fake-90s-news bulletin in the style of a BBS scrolltext (UPPERCASE, BREAKING NEWS markers, *** STAY TUNED ***, cyber attitude, demoscene flavor) and embed it as a JS template literal (backticks) rather than a single-quoted string, so apostrophes and quotation marks in the text can't accidentally break the code. Be playful.

Single HTML file using three.js from CDN. Classic horizontal greetz scroller with bouncing chars. Render the whole line as ONE CanvasTexture on a single scrolling plane (not one Sprite/Mesh per character — that gets expensive fast for a long greetz list) with per-character y-bounce and rainbow coloring baked into the canvas draw calls each frame: for character index i at canvas x-position px_i, draw it at y = baseline + sin(time*3 + i*0.4)*8 with fillStyle from an HSL rotation. For the text content: please invent your own list of ~30 fictional demo-group greetz (e.g. GREETZ TO THE ELECTRIC MONKS ... FUTURE CRACKERS ... ANSI ASYLUM) connected by separators like --- and ***, plus a closing signoff, embedded as a JS template literal (backticks) so any apostrophes in your made-up names can't break the code. Make up creative groups. Loop the text.

Star Wars-style perspective vertical text crawl: a long PlaneGeometry tilted ~45deg on the X axis receding into the distance, with a CanvasTexture of multi-paragraph text scrolling upward (offset.y increases with time; set texture.needsUpdate = true each redraw). Fade to black at the top via a gradient overlay. Single HTML file using three.js from CDN. Fullscreen plasma shader background cycling through magenta, cyan, and deep purple, with a transparent 2D canvas overlay that displays a poem one stanza at a time. Track a simple state machine: currentStanza, and a timer that fades opacity from 0 to 1 over 1s, holds for 4s, fades back to 0 over 1s, then advances to the next stanza (loop back to the first after the last) — 6 seconds total per stanza. Render the text in soft cream with a faint glow. For the content: please write your own original 4-stanza poem about light, math, and the strange beauty of small machines; store the stanzas as an array of JS template literals (backticks) so punctuation in the poem can't break the code. Use a font that feels like an old Amiga BBS.

Single HTML file using three.js from CDN. Matrix-style green code rain via a fullscreen ShaderMaterial sampling a glyph atlas CanvasTexture: draw an NxN grid of glyphs (katakana + ASCII, CRT-style monospace font) onto one canvas up front, and in the shader pick a cell via floor(random*N) and look up its UV sub-rectangle to sample the right glyph. Periodically (every ~12s) the rain dims for a few seconds and a horizontal text crawl fades in across the middle of the screen via a separate canvas overlay. For the content: please invent your own list of cryptic, half-prophetic system messages (e.g. KERNEL DREAMS IN HEXADECIMAL, CHECKSUM OF THE HEART: 0xDEADC0DE) as a JS array of template literals (backticks) so punctuation can't break the code; rotate to a new one each time the rain dims.

Single HTML file using three.js from CDN. Black background, monospace text printed line-by-line at the top with typewriter timing (~30ms per character) on a 2D canvas overlay; behind it, a slow plasma fullscreen shader. For the content: please write your own ~40 lines of fake retro boot/POST messages mixing real flavor (MEMORY TEST: 65536 OK, INITIALIZING IRQ HANDLERS) with absurd entries (CALIBRATING DREAM BUFFER, INJECTING VIBES...) stored as an array of JS template literals (backticks) so punctuation can't break the code. Single HTML file using three.js from CDN. Fullscreen ShaderMaterial with a glyph atlas CanvasTexture: draw an NxN grid of glyphs (katakana + ASCII in a green CRT font) onto one canvas once at startup, and pass its grid size N as a uniform so the shader can compute UV sub-rectangles. Pass an array of per-column speed and offset as a uniform (or pack them into a small 1D data texture). For each column, compute head = fract(time*speed[col] + offset[col]); intensity falls off the further a pixel is above the head (toward smaller y); pick a glyph cell that changes every ~100ms per row using a hash of (column, floor(time*10), row). Bright head = white; tail fades to dark green; black background.

Single HTML file using three.js from CDN. 200 BoxGeometry bars colored by value through an HSL palette. Implement bubble sort, quicksort, and merge sort each as a JS generator function that 'yield's after every single comparison-or-swap (this is the simplest reliable way to turn a sorting algorithm into an animation — don't try to hand-roll a custom step-by-step state machine per algorithm). Keep one 'currentSort' generator object; call currentSort.next() once per animation frame (or a few times per frame if you want faster sorting) and update the bar heights/positions and highlight colors from the yielded state. On generator completion (done:true), shuffle the array and create a new generator for the next algorithm in the rotation. Highlight the active indices in white. OrthographicCamera.

Single HTML file using three.js from CDN. Sun (SphereGeometry, MeshBasicMaterial yellow with a PointLight at its center) and 8 planets on circular orbits with scaled relative sizes and orbital speeds; Saturn gets a RingGeometry; Earth has a small moon orbiting it. Use exaggerated but readable scale (don't use true astronomical ratios or the inner planets become invisible dots next to Neptune's orbit) — e.g. orbit radii evenly spaced from 4 to 30 units, planet radii from 0.3 to 1.5 units. Position the camera far enough back and high enough (e.g. (0, 25, 45) looking at the origin) that the outermost orbit is fully in frame. Background of 2000 THREE.Points stars. Slow camera orbit; faint orbit Lines.

Single HTML file using three.js from CDN. SphereGeometry with many vertices (e.g. 64x64 segments); a vertex shader displaces each vertex along its normal by a value built from layered sine waves of (theta, phi, time), scaled so the maximum displacement is a modest fraction of the sphere's radius (e.g. up to 20%) — displacing further than that can invert the surface or push it through the camera, which looks broken or blank. Color by displacement magnitude through a deep-purple to electric-blue palette with bright white peaks. An EffectComposer + UnrealBloomPass glow is a nice finishing touch if you add it (import both from the same addons path as your importmap, and call composer.render() instead of renderer.render()), but keep it optional — the throbbing orb should still read clearly without it. Black background.

Single HTML file using three.js from CDN. A Rubik's cube as 27 small BoxGeometry cubies with per-face colors. Each second perform one face turn from a precomputed scramble; afterward play the reverse to solve. To animate a turn: create a temporary THREE.Group at the cube's center, use group.attach(cubie) (not group.add) for each of the 9 cubies on the turning face so their world transforms are preserved when they're reparented, slerp the group's quaternion over 0.4s to perform the turn, then scene.attach(cubie) each cubie back to the top-level scene afterward so the next turn's group starts clean. Slow camera orbit.

Single HTML file using three.js from CDN. Two helical paths position(t) = (cos(t)*r, t*pitch, sin(t)*r) and the mirrored partner. Place 100 base SphereGeometry instances along each strand connected by horizontal CylinderGeometry rungs. The full helix spans roughly height = 100*pitch, so position the camera back far enough to see the whole thing (e.g. distance ~1.5x the total height) and slowly rotate around Y. Color one strand bright cyan and the other strand bright magenta; cycle rung colors through the 4-color set red/green/blue/yellow to represent A/T/C/G. Black background with faint star points.

Single HTML file using three.js from CDN. PlaneGeometry 40x40 with 200x200 segments. A vertex shader displaces position.z by a sum of negative Gaussians at N orbiting mass points: z -= sum_i mass_i * exp(-dist_i^2 / sigma), with sigma large enough (e.g. 4.0) that even at closest approach the displacement stays bounded and doesn't spike the grid through the camera. Masses orbit the origin on circles; passing close deepens wells. Render the grid as glowing cyan wireframe lines on a near-black background; tint the lines toward bright magenta where wells are deepest (use displacement depth to mix the color). Slow camera orbit.

Single HTML file using three.js from CDN. Build the 16 vertices of a 4D hypercube and its 32 edges. Each frame multiply vertices by a 4D rotation matrix in the XW and YW planes (angle = time*0.3), then project to 3D by w-perspective division (3 / (3 - v.w)). Render edges as LineSegments; color by edge index through a palette. Black background.

Single HTML file using three.js from CDN. A flat ground plane with a glowing magenta wireframe grid (LineSegments) scrolling toward the camera (offset.z increases each frame; when offset.z exceeds one grid cell, wrap it back so the scroll loops seamlessly). A huge low sun made of horizontal magenta-to-yellow gradient bars rising on the horizon. Sky gradient from deep indigo at the top through hot pink to bright orange near the horizon. Tiny THREE.Points white stars fade in higher up. Camera locked in classic synthwave low perspective. A slight bloom via EffectComposer + UnrealBloomPass is a nice finishing VHS-glow touch if you add it (import both from the same addons path as your importmap), but keep it optional — the scene must still look complete with plain rendering if you skip it.

Single HTML file using three.js from CDN. Several tall PlaneGeometry curtains placed at varying depths in front of a starry sky. Each curtain uses a fragment shader that draws vertical flowing color bands modulated by 2-octave noise (define a small inline value-noise function yourself) scrolling sideways with time. Color the bands from bright lime-green at the bottom, through electric teal, into deep violet at the top, with occasional pink flares. Use additive blending so overlapping curtains brighten. Background: very deep navy sky filled with white pinprick THREE.Points stars; faint silhouette of jagged mountains at the horizon.

Single HTML file using three.js from CDN. Fullscreen ShaderMaterial. Fragment shader implements Voronoi: 32 feature points whose positions drift via sin/cos of time on different orbits; for each pixel find the nearest two points and use F2-F1 (edge distance) as the value. Map it through a smooth palette: deep indigo at cell centers, bright cyan at edges, blinding white right on the seams. Cells expand, contract, and merge organically. OrthographicCamera.

Single HTML file using three.js from CDN. A triangular grid of small SphereGeometry pegs (15 rows) drawn in soft grey, positions computed once at startup. Each frame spawn a new ball at the top with a tiny random horizontal nudge; integrate gravity, and when a ball's position comes within its radius of a peg, deflect it deterministically based on which side of the peg it's on (left half of the peg -> nudge left and flip vertical velocity to a small bounce, right half -> nudge right) rather than a random per-collision coin flip — this keeps balls from getting stuck oscillating on a peg. Balls accumulate in vertical bins at the bottom (stop integrating a ball once it settles, snapping it into a neat stack within its bin) gradually forming a bell curve. Color balls by their final bin position through a warm-to-cool palette: red in the leftmost bins, through yellow and green, to cyan in the rightmost. Dark charcoal background.
